subChunks.title: Figma Variables Pipeline
subChunks.hookHtml: The gap between design and code is measured in token drift. A designer updates a colour in Figma. The developer updates a different shade in the codebase. Six months later, there are three slightly different values of 'primary blue' in the product. A Figma Variables pipeline — Figma Variables → token export → CSS custom properties → Tailwind @theme — eliminates this drift by making design tokens a single-source-of-truth artifact that flows from tool to tool without human transcription.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Sable the Illuminator: "The pipeline exists because humans transcribe incorrectly. Not through carelessness — through the inherent ambiguity of converting visual values to code. Indigo-600 in Figma might be #4f46e5. The developer sees it and picks text-indigo-600. But the designer also has a 'Primary' variable pointing to a custom value. Without a pipeline, you have two colours that look similar but aren't the same."

Figma Variables → Design Token JSON

Figma Variables (introduced 2023) expose design tokens as JSON via the REST API or plugins:

// tokens.json (exported from Figma via Token Studio or Figma Tokens plugin)
{
  "color": {
    "brand": {
      "$type": "color",
      "$value": "oklch(0.55 0.20 270)",
      "$description": "Primary brand colour"
    },
    "surface": {
      "$type": "color",
      "$value": "{color.neutral.50}",
      "$description": "Default page background"
    }
  },
  "spacing": {
    "4": { "$type": "dimension", "$value": "16px" },
    "8": { "$type": "dimension", "$value": "32px" }
  }
}

Style Dictionary — token transformer

// style-dictionary.config.mjs
import StyleDictionary from 'style-dictionary';

export default {
  source: ['tokens/**/*.json'],
  platforms: {
    css: {
      transformGroup: 'css',
      prefix: '',
      buildPath: 'src/styles/',
      files: [{
        destination: 'tokens.css',
        format: 'css/variables',
        options: {
          outputReferences: true,
          selector: ':root',
        }
      }]
    }
  }
};

// Output: src/styles/tokens.css
:root {
  --color-brand: oklch(0.55 0.20 270);
  --color-surface: var(--color-neutral-50);
  --spacing-4: 16px;
  --spacing-8: 32px;
}

Bridging Style Dictionary output to Tailwind @theme

/* globals.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "./styles/tokens.css";  /* Style Dictionary output */

/* Map CSS custom properties to Tailwind @theme tokens */
@theme {
  --color-primary: var(--color-brand);
  --color-surface: var(--color-surface);  /* Already a custom prop */
  --spacing-4: var(--spacing-4);

  /* Or: reference the generated vars directly in utilities */
  /* bg-[var(--color-brand)] works without @theme mapping */
}

/* Now: bg-primary, text-primary, border-primary */
/* AND: bg-[var(--color-brand)] as a fallback */

Automated pipeline with CI

# .github/workflows/tokens.yml
name: Sync Design Tokens
on:
  push:
    paths: ['tokens/**']

jobs:
  build-tokens:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm install
      - run: npx style-dictionary build
      - name: Open PR if tokens changed
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6
        with:
          title: 'chore: sync design tokens from Figma'
          body: 'Automated token sync'
          branch: 'chore/token-sync'

W3C Design Token Format (DTF)

The W3C Design Token Community Group is standardising the token JSON format:

// W3C DTF (draft standard) — what Figma Variables exports target
{
  "Brand Blue": {
    "$type": "color",
    "$value": "#0047AB"
  },
  "Spacing Medium": {
    "$type": "dimension",
    "$value": "16px"
  }
}
// This is the format Style Dictionary v4 natively supports

Sable: "The pipeline is the contract between design and engineering. When a designer changes a token in Figma, it creates a PR. An engineer reviews it. The change is intentional and tracked. No more 'I updated the colour in the mockup but forgot to tell dev.' The pipeline makes that omission structurally impossible."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: The Figma Variables pipeline removes the human from the transcription step. Designers change a token. A script runs. A PR opens. An engineer reviews. The change lands in the codebase exactly as designed — no interpretation, no drift, no 'I thought it was indigo-500.'

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design a complete Figma Variables pipeline architecture diagram from scratch. Show: the Figma Variables export step (format, tool), the Style Dictionary transformation step (config, output format), the Tailwind @theme mapping step, the CI automation step (trigger, PR creation), and where semantic vs primitive tokens live in the chain. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the Figma Variables → Style Dictionary → Tailwind @theme pipeline end-to-end. What problem does it solve? What is the role of each tool in the chain? What happens when a designer updates a token in Figma — walk through exactly what occurs in the pipeline and what the final effect is in the codebase.

questions.prompt: What problem does a Figma Variables → CSS tokens pipeline solve?
options: Token drift — prevents designers and developers from maintaining separate, diverging values for the same design tokens
Bundle size — reduces CSS file size by sharing tokens across design tools and codebases
Type safety — generates TypeScript types from Figma variables for use in component props
Version control — makes Figma designs version-controllable via Git
questions.answer: Token drift — prevents designers and developers from maintaining separate, diverging values for the same design tokens
questions.explanation: Token drift is the primary problem: without a pipeline, designers update tokens in Figma and developers maintain separate values in code. Over months, these diverge — there are three slightly different 'primary blues' across the product. A pipeline makes Figma the single source of truth and exports tokens programmatically, eliminating human transcription errors.

questions.prompt: Style Dictionary outputs --color-brand: oklch(0.55 0.20 270) in a :root CSS block. How do you make Tailwind generate bg-brand and text-brand utility classes from this value?
options: In @theme: --color-brand: var(--color-brand) — this maps the CSS custom property to a Tailwind token, which generates the bg-brand, text-brand, etc. utilities
Add brand to the extend.colors section of tailwind.config.js pointing to the CSS variable
Tailwind automatically detects :root CSS variables and generates utilities — no mapping needed
Use @utility to manually define .bg-brand { background-color: var(--color-brand); }
questions.answer: In @theme: --color-brand: var(--color-brand) — this maps the CSS custom property to a Tailwind token, which generates the bg-brand, text-brand, etc. utilities
questions.explanation: In Tailwind v4, @theme is the mechanism that bridges CSS custom properties to utility class generation. By adding --color-brand: var(--color-brand) to @theme, you tell Tailwind to create a color token named 'brand' whose value comes from the CSS variable. Tailwind then generates the full family of colour utilities: bg-brand, text-brand, border-brand, shadow-brand, ring-brand, etc.

questions.prompt: A team exports Figma Variables as JSON and manually copies values into Tailwind @theme every sprint. A colleague proposes automating this with Style Dictionary + a GitHub Action. What is the main benefit beyond saving time?
options: Determinism — the automated pipeline applies the same transformation rules every time, preventing human errors like typos, rounding differences, or accidentally using the wrong colour mode
Speed — CI pipelines run faster than manual copying, reducing build times
Type safety — Style Dictionary generates TypeScript interfaces that manual copying cannot
Versioning — CI automation creates a commit history for token changes
questions.answer: Determinism — the automated pipeline applies the same transformation rules every time, preventing human errors like typos, rounding differences, or accidentally using the wrong colour mode
questions.explanation: The primary value of automation is not speed — it's determinism. A human copying oklch(0.55 0.20 270) might type oklch(0.55 0.20 27) (dropping a digit). They might use the light-mode value when they should use the dark-mode value. They might apply rounded values instead of exact values. An automated pipeline applies exactly the same transformation rules every time, making the result predictable and auditable. Version history (answer D) is also a valid benefit but is secondary to correctness.
